{{Short description|none}}
Historians of mathematics have noted the involvement of prominent mathematicians in politics at various times and places, notably in [[Italy]] during the period of [[Italian unification|unification]] at the end of the nineteenth century.<ref name=Durand>{{cite journal |last1=Durand |first1=Antonin |title=Mathematicians and politics: new research scenarios? |journal=Lettera Matematica |date=March 2017 |volume=4 |issue=3–4 |pages=161–165 |publisher=Springer Milan |issn=2281-5937|doi=10.1007/s40329-016-0149-x |s2cid=151442761 }}</ref>

Those who become legislators attempt to use their mathematical skills to legitimise their political positions.<ref name=Durand/> However, some parliamentary colleagues tend to view them as failing to connect with the real world.<ref name=Durand/>

A maths columnist for ''[[Forbes]]'' suggested in 2018 that mathematicians in politics would contribute strengths including problem-solving, creativity, overcoming challenges, and collaboration.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crowell |first1=Rachel |title=Mathematicians Would Make Great Elected Officials. Here's Why |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/rachelcrowell/2018/08/24/mathematicians-would-make-great-elected-officials-heres-why |work=Forbes |accessdate=23 July 2019 |date=24 August 2018}}</ref>

[[John Derbyshire]] observed in 2003 that mathematicians have no dominant tendency; for example, [[Cauchy]] was a [[reactionary]] whereas [[Galois]] was a [[Political radicalism|radical]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Derbyshire |first1=John |title=Politics, Religion, and ''Prime Obsession'' |url=http://www.olimu.com/Riemann/PoliticsAndReligion.htm |date=October 2003 |accessdate=23 July 2019 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20050207205256/http://www.olimu.com/Riemann/PoliticsAndReligion.htm |archivedate=2005-02-07|url-status=dead}}</ref> He opines that the most influential research mathematicians do not give much thought to politics.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Derbyshire |first1=John |title=The Politics of Mathematicians |url=https://www.nationalreview.com/corner/politics-mathematicians-john-derbyshire/ |website=National Review |accessdate=23 July 2019 |date=12 February 2005}}</ref>

==Notable mathematician-politicians==
{{Incomplete list|date=June 2021}}
